description: ​Solo developer operating SSTO Kepler Dynamics for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (KL). Building an advanced, interactive Space Mission Design Game featuring real-time engineering trade-off logic, mass/budget constraints, and a sleek command-center UI. Passionate about aerospace systems and simulation software!
summary: KEPLER-1: Mission Control Simulator, built by SSTO Kepler Dynamics, is an interactive spacecraft systems engineering platform created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It addresses the challenge of teaching integrated space mission design by placing players in the role of a NASA Flight Director tasked with architecting end-to-end orbital and interplanetary missions across three distinct scenarios: LEO Earth Observation, Lunar South Pole Prospector, and Mars Reconnaissance. Players select real launch vehicles (Delta II, Atlas V, and SLS Block 1) and configure spacecraft buses, solar arrays, RTGs, propulsion systems, communications antennas, and scientific payloads while balancing competing trade-offs in mass, budget, electrical power, eclipse battery survival, delta-v, and downlink bandwidth. Benchmarked against flagship NASA missions (Terra EOS, LRO, and MRO) and powered by a real-time NASA Concept Maturity Level (CML 1–4) diagnostic engine and dynamic anomaly simulator, KEPLER-1 transforms abstract aerospace equations into an accessible, hands-on engineering environment that bridges the gap between textbook physics and real-world mission operations
details:
KEPLER-1 is a browser-based aerospace simulation platform where users select from three mission profiles—LEO Earth Observation, Lunar South Pole Prospector, and Mars Reconnaissance—each benchmarked against real NASA missions (Terra EOS, LRO, and MRO) and launch vehicles (Delta II, Atlas V, and SLS Block 1). As players assemble subsystems in the Modular Assembly Bay, a custom physics engine evaluates their design in real time:

  • Propulsion & Mass: Calculates achievable velocity change using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation (Δv = Isp × g₀ × ln(m₀/m₁)) against launch vehicle fairing limits.
  • Power & Eclipse Survival: Scales solar array generation by inverse-square solar flux (43% at Mars) and verifies whether onboard batteries (at 80% depth of discharge) survive orbital umbra periods.
  • Communications & Data: Evaluates instrument data generation against X-Band or Ka-Band downlink capacities adjusted for interplanetary range derating.
  • Live Orbital Visualization & Anomalies: Renders real-time 2D/3D orbital trajectories showing sunlit charging versus umbra battery drain, while an anomaly injector tests resilience against mid-mission crises like Solar Flares, Telemetry Buffer Overflows, and Eclipse Extensions.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Rather than simply flagging a design as right or wrong, KEPLER-1 implements NASA's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) alongside a structured ConOps (Concept of Operations) lifecycle and a root-cause engineering diagnostics engine. When a constraint fails, the simulator explains the exact physical bottleneck—such as battery brownouts in eclipse or recorder overflow from insufficient downlink bandwidth—and guides players on how to resolve it. Our goal is to make authentic systems engineering accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

How Our Project Is Creative

Instead of presenting space mission design as a dry spreadsheet or static quiz, KEPLER-1 gamifies real NASA systems engineering workflows into a live Mission Control environment. Combining an interactive orbital canvas that visually responds to eclipse shadows and validation errors, mid-flight anomaly injections, a multi-player Team Mode, and copyable Mission Engineering Reports turns complex aerospace math into an engaging, replayable strategy experience.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Accessibility Across Skill Levels: We designed three distinct gameplay modes—Cadet Mode (with interactive physics tooltips), Flight Director Mode (enforcing strict 10% budget/power reserves and 5% mass growth margins), and Sandbox Mode—so both beginners and advanced users can learn effectively.
  • Scientific Authenticity vs. Playability: We balanced real aerospace physics (Tsiolkovsky rocket math, inverse-square solar flux, and NASA CML 1–4 standards) with clean visual telemetry bars so complex trade-offs remain intuitive.
  • Usability & Compatibility: We built the simulator as a lightweight, self-contained web application with responsive layouts, Team Mode seat-passing, and reduced-motion accessibility support so anyone can run it smoothly on any device without installations.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Core Technologies: HTML5, JavaScript (ES6+), React 18, HTM (Hyperscript Tagged Markup), Tailwind CSS, and Three.js for 3D visualizations.
  • Graphics & Visualization: Custom HTML5 Canvas rendering engines for real-time orbital mechanics and eclipse telemetry.
  • Aerospace Frameworks & Reference Data: NASA Concept Maturity Level (CML 1–4) standards, Tsiolkovsky rocket equation modeling, and NASA mission hardware specifications (Terra EOS, LRO, MRO, Delta II, Atlas V, and SLS).
